paper.title: Charon: A Unified and Fine-Grained Simulator for Large-Scale LLM Training and Inference
paper.authors: Mengtian Yang, Zhekun Zhang, Mingheng Wu, Jianwen Yan, Hanshi Sun, Li-Wen Chang
paper.license: arXiv non-exclusive distribution licence (http://arxiv.org/licenses/nonexclusive-distrib/1.0/); figures reproduced as a style reference with attribution, copyright stays with the authors
paper.note: Added on user request (2026-10-09) as the reference for the named style 'charon'. Not part of the rated corpus: no aesthetic label, no corpus statistics are derived from it. Author figures are PowerPoint exports (Quartz PDFContext), so source.svg is the author PDF converted with text kept as <text>.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Charon enables end-to-end, operator-level simulation for LLM training and inference. It delivers more than 30k cost reduction compared with cluster profiling for large-scale experiment, with only 3.74% total training time error on a large-scale training task.

slots.why_chosen: Charon-style teaser: left half is the system as a stacked platform card fed by framework logos, right half two boxed result cards (cost, accuracy) that carry the claim in numbers.
slots.what_to_learn: Say the contribution three times in one column: a red 'old way' arrow versus a green 'with us' label over the same input/output, a grey platform card holding three full-width pastel capability bars, and two black-framed side cards with one number each in the same red/green.

semantics.summary: The teaser contrasts two ways to find a good training or inference configuration for a native model: profiling-based tuning on a real GPU cluster (red route, $1k per evaluation) and design exploration with the Charon simulation platform (green route, a few cents). The platform is a grey rounded card listing three capabilities as full-width pastel bars; two framed cards on the right state the cost saving (>30k x) and the accuracy (-3.74% versus profiling).
semantics.summary_zh: 引言配图：左边是同一个模型的两条调参路线，红色是上集群实测（每次约 1000 美元），绿色是用 Charon 仿真；Charon 画成灰色圆角平台卡，里面三条通栏浅色条列出三项能力。右边两张黑框小卡分别给出成本（省 3 万倍以上）和精度（误差 3.74%）。

figures.caption: Figure 2: LLM architecture, execution workflows, and tuning challenges: (a) Decoder-only Transformer stack with QKV attention and optional MoE in the feed-forward layers. (b) Training (forward, backward, update) and inference (prefill, decode with KV cache) workflows alongside key parallelism schemes. (c) Iterative profiling-based tuning loop and its GPU-hour/design-space explosion on large GPU clusters.

slots.why_chosen: A whole background section in one tall single-column figure: three black-framed bands (a)-(c), each split by a dash-dot rule into a diagram and its companion (zoomed block, parallelism catalogue, motivation chart).
slots.what_to_learn: Frame each panel with one thick black rectangle and a bold (a)/(b)/(c) in its top-left corner, split a panel with a dash-dot vertical rule, and keep one fill per concept across panels (blue = transformer block / forward, pink = backward / K / layer, peach = output / V, mint = norm / expected).

slots.why_chosen: Panel (a) zooms one Transformer block of a grey/blue layer stack into a pale-blue detail box with two converging guide lines.
slots.what_to_learn: Draw the zoom as two straight lines from the selected stack box to the corners of a tinted detail box; inside it, rotated tall bars (Norm Layer) act as section dividers.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Architecture overview of proposed Charon simulator. The system consists of a graph-based frontend that constructs forward and backward computation graphs while applying optimizations and analyses; a multi-engine backend that accurately simulates both computation and communication operators; and a design explorer that searches for the optimal configuration through guided pruning.

slots.why_chosen: The canonical Charon-style overview: inputs on the left, the platform as one big rounded frame with three equal subsystem boxes, outputs on the right, the whole thing inside a thick black outer frame.
slots.what_to_learn: Title each flank and each subsystem with bold text, put the subsystem name at the bottom of its box, open each subsystem with a grey header bar, and fill only the leaves with the role colours (blue / peach / mint / pink); tiny glyphs (node-link graphs, timeline bars, a pruned tree) stand in for what each stage produces.

system.name: Charon
system.one_liner: a unified, operator-level simulator that predicts LLM training and inference performance so configurations can be explored without cluster profiling

components.name: Input Description
components.role: left flank: Native Model (Hugging Face, vLLM, Custom PyTorch logos) + System Config (GPU/NPU info, interconnect, parallelism plan)

components.name: Graph-based Frontend
components.role: model information + configuration -> graph generation (Linear, Matmul, Scale, Softmax) -> graph manipulation -> graph execution producing a trace

components.name: Multi-engine Backend
components.role: operator simulator with profiling, prediction and analytical (computation / communication) engines joined by a fused engine, plus an op overlap processor

components.name: Design Explorer
components.role: design parameters as a search tree pruned by a rule-based pruning tool

components.name: Simulation Results
components.role: right flank: simulation summary (latency, flops / MFU, memory, power), timeline trace (single layer, 3D), design exploration (best config)

content.key_idea: One platform turns a native model plus a system config into an operator graph, simulates every operator with the cheapest accurate engine, and searches configurations by pruning.
content.reading_order: Left flank inputs -> frontend (top-down inside) -> backend -> design explorer -> right flank outputs.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Frontend architecture of proposed Charon simulator. (a) Trace and generate forward and backward groups from native PyTorch models. (b) Apply compiler-style passes for optimizations and analyses.

slots.why_chosen: Two stacked panels separated by a dash-dot rule: (a) a tracing pipeline from a native model to forward / backward graphs, (b) three tinted dotted pass groups between two rotated grey bookend bars.
slots.what_to_learn: Use rotated grey bars as the input and output bookends of a pass pipeline, give each pass family a pale dotted region (peach / blue / pink) holding white rounded steps with vertical ellipses, and draw graphs as pastel node-link glyphs coloured by direction (blue forward, pink backward).

slots.why_chosen: Panel (b) is a left-to-right pipeline of three pass groups whose steps run top-down inside each group.
slots.what_to_learn: Hand off between groups with an elbow arrow from the last step of one group to the first of the next.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Backend architecture of Charon simulator. Each operator can be simulated using a profiling, prediction, or analytical engine. A fused backend enables mixed-engine execution, allowing different operators to be simulated by different engines.

slots.why_chosen: Each engine is a full-height tinted panel in its identity colour (blue / peach sharing one panel, mint, grey), and the fused engine on the right re-uses the same three colours as its decision boxes.
slots.what_to_learn: Tint the whole panel, not just a header, with the subsystem's identity colour, put white boxes inside, and let a later decision flow refer back to each subsystem by a dotted box in that same tint; Y / N labels on the branches.

system.name: Charon

components.name: Profiling Engine
components.role: operator type + shape -> profile on GPU -> profiling database lookup

components.name: Prediction Engine
components.role: profiling database trains a random-forest predictor for unseen shapes

figures.caption: Figure 6: Bandwidth-aware communication operators overlap in the proposed Charon simulator, (a) shows the timeline of original communication operations, and (b) shows the timeline with congestion-aware simulation.

slots.why_chosen: Before/after on the same time axis with worked bandwidth values: (a) every communication op at full speed, (b) the same ops slowed down where they overlap, with the bandwidth arithmetic written beside the rows.
slots.what_to_learn: Encode the link by hue (green NVLink, blue IB) and the state by fill strength plus outline (solid saturated = full speed, pale dotted = slowed down), give the legend as two arrow-pairs above the axis, and write the congestion arithmetic in the link's own colour next to the rows it explains.

figures.caption: Figure 12: Illustration of zigzag attention and dynamic SP planning. Each request can adopt a different SP configuration: request 1 adopts SP4, and request 2 adopts SP2 with zigzag.

slots.why_chosen: Per-rank operator timelines without and with dynamic SP, coloured by request (blue shades = request 1, red = request 2), ending in a dashed deadline line and a 'Saved Time' double arrow.
slots.what_to_learn: Colour the work by whom it belongs to, not by operator; split a bar's fill when one operator serves two requests; mark the gain as a dashed vertical finish line plus a labelled double-headed arrow.

slots.why_chosen: Panel (a) explains zigzag attention as KV chunk strips and causal-mask triangles per rank, with circled chunk numbers and a shade ramp.
slots.what_to_learn: Number chunks with circled digits and give each chunk one step of a single-hue shade ramp so the reader can follow it from the strip into the mask cells.

semantics.summary: (a) Zigzag attention: KV chunks 1-4 are all-gathered so that rank 0 computes chunks 1 and 4 and rank 1 chunks 2 and 3 of the causal mask. (b) Per-rank operator timelines for two requests: with SP4 zigzag for both, every rank runs both requests' attention and a second all-gather; with dynamic SP (request 1 SP4, request 2 SP2), ranks 2-3 skip request 2 and the batch finishes earlier, marked by a saved-time arrow.
semantics.summary_zh: 案例图：(a) zigzag 注意力怎么把 KV 块分给两个 rank；(b) 每个 rank 的算子时间线，按请求着色（蓝是请求 1、红是请求 2），对比统一 SP4 和按请求选 SP 两种做法，最后用虚线和双箭头标出省下的时间。
